t: Margin vs markup: price your products without losing money
d: The difference between margin and markup, conversion tables, how GST fits into your selling price, and how discounts quietly eat margin, with worked examples.
x: "I keep 25% on everything." Two shopkeepers can say this and mean very different things. One means markup, the other means margin, and the difference can wipe out a year's profit. The two definitions Markup is profit as a percentage of cost . Margin is profit as a percentage of selling price . Example: you buy an item for ₹80 and sell it for ₹100. Profit is ₹20. Markup = 20 ÷ 80 = 25% Margin = 20 ÷ 100 = 20% Same item, same profit, two different percentages. Margin is always lower than markup. d: Find your profit margin and markup from cost and selling price, or set a selling price from a target margin or markup. Shows the price to charge including GST.
x: I know the Selling price Target margin Markup Cost price per unit (₹, before GST) Selling price (before GST) GST rate on the product (%, optional) No GST / composition 5% 18% 40% 3% Gross margin 0% Margin or markup? Margin = Profit ÷ Selling price × 100. Markup = Profit ÷ Cost × 100. An item bought for ₹600 and sold for ₹800 makes ₹200 profit: a 25% margin but a 33.3% markup. If you want a 25% margin, you cannot simply add 25% to cost; that gives ₹750 and only a 20% margin. Price for a target margin = Cost ÷ (1 − Margin ÷ 100). For a 25% margin on ₹600: 600 ÷ 0.75 = ₹800.
